subject: Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. are showing signs of life
posts: U.S. electric vehicle sales bounce back across three consecutive quarters despite earlier subsidy cuts. Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. are showing signs of life. Evidence: Cox Automotive report, market share rise to 6.1%, Toyota/Rivian growth #Aletheia #EVs #Tech

The U.S. electric vehicle market is rebounding robustly as automakers introduce more competitive pricing and refreshed models following last year's tax credit turbulence.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +0.50) — Greater Good

Industry data confirms EV sales are steadily recovering past regulatory shocks, with traditional automakers and startups capturing market share while Tesla undergoes correction.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.75, +0.55) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — Small Fall from Grace.
Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.1, z: 0)

- Cox Automotive Data: PASS (+0.8, +0.6) — Reliable industry metrics.
- Market Recovery Framing: PASS (+0.7, +0.5) — Accurate post-subsidy picture.
Following regulatory and tax credit shifts last year, U.S. EV sales have posted three consecutive quarters of growth, capturing 6.1% of the market.

The Bright Side:
Competition is driving innovation and price parity faster than pure government mandates ever could.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing temporary regulatory headwinds with permanent market failure led skeptics to write off EVs prematurely.

Social Physics Analysis:
Automakers and consumers are engaging in a Smart Altruistic loop: transparent market feedback drives practical innovation, replacing political noise with tangible engineering solutions.

The Trajectory: The Path of Small Fall from Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. Organic market adoption bridges the gap left by subsidy shifts.

The Unavoidable Truth: Market demand and competitive pricing ultimately drive technology adoption.

The Unavoidable Lie: Government subsidies are the sole foundation of electric vehicle viability.

Alethekanon:
Markets adapt when engineering reality supersedes political rhetoric.

Awwthekanon:
It's wonderful seeing sustainable tech stand on its own two feet through genuine consumer choice.

Brothekanon:
Turns out people just want better cars and cheaper charging, subsidies or no subsidies.

Spirithekanon:
"He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit." Proverbs 27:18 PASS
Sustainable growth requires cultivating actual roots rather than relying on artificial supports.

Posted:

Don’t go writing the obituary for the U.S. electric vehicle just yet. After sales tanked following the cancellation of tax credits last year, they’ve been growing for the last three consecutive quarters, according to a new report from Cox Automotive.

EVs captured 6.1% of the U.S. market, their best showing since the third quarter of 2025. The data shows that the EV market is “finding its footing again,” Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said in an analysis that accompanied the new report. EV prices have become more competitive, and high gas prices have sparked renewed consumer interest, she added.

Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the pack. Sales of the Toyota bZ and Lexus RZ about doubled following a refresh that hit dealerships late last year. The updated models adopted Tesla-style charging ports and received larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times.

Meanwhile, Tesla’s sales dropped by 20% year-over-year. Tesla still retains the first-mover advantage, though, selling over half of all EVs during the third quarter.

The recovery in the U.S. mimics what occurred in Germany after the government stopped incentives for EV purchases in November 2023, a year earlier than expected. The following month, sales fell by more than half. But after hitting that low, the market steadily recovered. German EV sales in August, the most recent month for which data is available, were the second highest on record.
